name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
course: Look beyond the recent diary: persistent symptoms for six months, signs before age 12, and difficulties in more than one setting.

checklist.label: Attention during ordinary tasks
checklist.question: Which tasks are difficult to finish, and what happens when you try?

checklist.label: Activity and impulse control
checklist.question: When is waiting or slowing down difficult?

checklist.label: Childhood pattern
checklist.question: What do earlier school reports or caregivers recall before age 12?

checklist.label: Different settings and consequences
checklist.question: How does this affect responsibilities at home and school or work?

checklist.label: Sleep, health and learning context
checklist.question: When did sleep, mood or learning difficulties appear compared with the attention problems?

test.name: Structured developmental ADHD assessment
test.purpose: Combine current examples, childhood records and reports across settings.
test.interpretation: No single test establishes ADHD. Age-appropriate ratings assist a qualified assessment; checklist completion is not diagnosis.

cautions: Use child/caregiver and school accounts together. Recent adult attention loss requires a broader medical and mood review.

sources.title: NIMH: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
CDC: Diagnosing ADHD

name: Autism spectrum disorder
course: Assess an early developmental pattern, including differences that become noticeable only as demands increase; recent simulated events do not establish onset.

checklist.label: Social communication across contexts
checklist.question: Which parts of conversation or understanding people take extra effort?

checklist.label: Routines, interests and repetitive patterns
checklist.question: What happens when a familiar routine changes?

checklist.label: Sensory experiences
checklist.question: Which sounds, textures or environments are unusually difficult or helpful?

checklist.label: Early development and collateral
checklist.question: What do caregivers or early records tell us about communication and play?

checklist.label: Strengths, functioning and support
checklist.question: What works well for you, and what support makes daily life easier?

differentials: Intellectual developmental disability, which can coexist

test.name: Comprehensive developmental autism assessment
test.purpose: Integrate observation, developmental history, communication and adaptive functioning.
test.interpretation: Screening identifies a need for evaluation; neither a brief checklist nor fluent text establishes or excludes autism.

cautions: For toddlers use caregiver history and observed play; do not infer intelligence, empathy or support needs from speech style.

sources.title: NIMH: Autism spectrum disorder
CDC: Screening for autism spectrum disorder

name: Specific learning disorder
course: School-age difficulties persist despite targeted help for at least six months; adult recognition still requires educational history.

checklist.label: Specific academic difficulty
checklist.question: Which reading, writing or number tasks remain hard even with practice?

checklist.label: Response to targeted support
checklist.question: What teaching or support has been tried, and what changed?

checklist.label: School history
checklist.question: When were these difficulties first noticed?

checklist.label: Practical impact
checklist.question: How do these tasks affect school, work or everyday independence?

checklist.label: Learning opportunity and language
checklist.question: What languages and teaching opportunities were available, and have hearing or vision been assessed?

differentials: Inadequate educational opportunity or unfamiliar instructional language

test.name: Comprehensive psychoeducational assessment
test.purpose: Combine achievement assessment, school records and response to instruction.
test.interpretation: Standardized results need developmental and educational interpretation; low grades alone are not a diagnosis.

cautions: Do not equate learning disability with low intelligence. Interpret assessments in the person's language and educational context.

sources.title: APA: What are specific learning disorders?

name: Language disorder
course: Developmental language difficulties may persist into adulthood; evaluate the early history rather than treating a short conversation as a language test.

checklist.label: Understanding language
checklist.question: Which instructions or kinds of explanations are difficult to follow?

checklist.label: Expressing ideas
checklist.question: When is it hard to find words or tell someone what happened?

checklist.label: Early language development
checklist.question: How did speech and understanding develop when you were younger?

checklist.label: All languages and hearing
checklist.question: Which languages do you use, and are difficulties similar in each?

checklist.label: Communication impact
checklist.question: How does this affect learning, relationships or getting needs met?

differentials: Language exposure or multilingual assessment mismatch

test.name: Speech-language pathology assessment
test.purpose: Use observation, language sampling, informant accounts and suitable standardized measures.
test.interpretation: Assessment describes language needs and informs diagnosis; a chatbot transcript is not a standardized language assessment.

cautions: Multilingualism does not cause language disorder. NIDCD's DLD terminology is related to, but not automatically identical with, every DSM language-disorder presentation.

sources.title: NIDCD: Developmental language disorder

name: Intellectual developmental disorder (intellectual disability)
course: Intellectual and adaptive limitations begin during development; acquired decline later in life requires a different evaluation.

checklist.label: Learning and reasoning history
checklist.question: What kinds of learning have needed repeated support since childhood?

checklist.label: Practical daily skills
checklist.question: Which daily activities can you do independently, and where is help useful?

checklist.label: Communication and social understanding
checklist.question: What helps with understanding information and navigating social situations?

checklist.label: Developmental records
checklist.question: What earlier assessments or caregiver observations are available?

checklist.label: Strengths and access
checklist.question: What skills and interests are strengths, and what barriers make tasks harder?

test.name: Intellectual and adaptive-functioning assessment
test.purpose: Pair culturally appropriate cognitive evaluation with everyday skills and informant history; adaptive tools may include Vineland scales.
test.interpretation: A score alone is insufficient. Qualified interpretation of both functioning domains and developmental onset is required.

cautions: Do not infer intellectual ability from limited speech. Very young children need developmental assessment; avoid invented IQ scores or support levels.

sources.title: APA: What is intellectual disability?

name: Tourette's disorder (Tourette syndrome)
course: Establish childhood onset before 18 and more than a year since tics began; motor and vocal tics may change or fluctuate.

checklist.label: Motor and vocal tic history
checklist.question: What repeated movements or sounds have occurred, even if they are absent today?

checklist.label: Age at onset and changing course
checklist.question: When did the first tic appear, and how has the pattern changed?

checklist.label: Experience around tics
checklist.question: What do you notice before a tic or when trying to hold it back?

checklist.label: Pain and participation
checklist.question: Do tics affect comfort, school, work or interactions?

checklist.label: Medical and medication context
checklist.question: What medicines, illnesses or other movements need to be considered?

differentials: Persistent motor or vocal tic disorder
Functional tic-like symptoms or neurological/medication effects

test.name: Clinical tic and developmental assessment
test.purpose: Review tic types, chronology, observation and possible alternative causes.
test.interpretation: A clinician interprets the pattern; text descriptions cannot substitute for examining movement symptoms.

cautions: Swearing is not required. Lack of impairment does not by itself exclude Tourette's; sudden new tic-like symptoms need appropriate assessment.

sources.title: CDC: Diagnosing tic disorders

name: Major depressive disorder
course: Explore a depressive episode lasting at least two weeks alongside the lifetime mood history; diary length alone cannot establish an episode.

checklist.label: Mood and loss of enjoyment
checklist.question: How have your mood and enjoyment changed from your usual self?

checklist.label: Episode continuity
checklist.question: When did this change begin, and has it been present most days?

checklist.label: Sleep, energy and thinking
checklist.question: What has changed in sleep, appetite, energy or concentration?

checklist.label: Daily functioning
checklist.question: Which responsibilities or relationships have become difficult?

checklist.label: Safety and hopelessness
checklist.question: Have you had thoughts about dying or harming yourself, and do you feel safe now?

checklist.label: Past elevation and other explanations
checklist.question: Have there been separate periods of unusually high energy with little need for sleep, or health or substance changes?

test.name: APA depression severity measure (adapted PHQ-9)
test.purpose: Record recent adult depressive symptom burden alongside an interview.
test.interpretation: This linked adaptation uses seven days. It supports severity assessment, not definitive diagnosis; use an appropriate adolescent version for youth.

cautions: Adolescents may describe irritability. Safety concerns require direct assessment regardless of any score.

sources.title: NIMH: Depression
APA: Adult depression severity measure, adapted PHQ-9

name: Persistent depressive disorder
course: Chronic depressed mood usually spans at least two years in adults, or one year in children/adolescents; investigate better intervals and superimposed episodes.

checklist.label: Long-term mood baseline
checklist.question: How long has feeling low been part of your usual life?

checklist.label: Periods of improvement
checklist.question: What was the longest time you felt more like yourself?

checklist.label: Energy and self-view
checklist.question: Over those years, how have energy, confidence and hope changed?

checklist.label: More intense episodes
checklist.question: Were there separate stretches when things became substantially worse or unusually energized?

checklist.label: Functioning and safety
checklist.question: What has this cost you in daily life, and have you felt unsafe or wished not to be alive?

test.name: Longitudinal mood assessment
test.purpose: Build a timeline using the person's history and available collateral.
test.interpretation: A short symptom scale can describe current severity but cannot prove a chronic course or definitively diagnose PDD.

cautions: Do not describe every chronic depression as mild. Review safety and the possibility of major episodes; a 28-day diary cannot supply years of evidence.

sources.title: APA: Depression and related conditions
NIMH: Depression

name: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD)
course: Review at least a year of persistent irritability and frequent severe outbursts; APA specifies onset before 10 and first diagnosis between 6 and 18.

checklist.label: Outburst frequency and context
checklist.question: Walk me through a recent outburst and what happened just before it.

checklist.label: Mood between outbursts
checklist.question: What is mood like on an ordinary day between these episodes?

checklist.label: Onset and longer well periods
checklist.question: When did this start, and were there several months when it stopped?

checklist.label: Home, school and peer settings
checklist.question: What do caregivers, teachers and the child each notice?

checklist.label: Distinct high-energy episodes
checklist.question: Has there been a separate period of unusually high energy and much less need for sleep?

test.name: Affective Reactivity Index (ARI), age-appropriate form
test.purpose: Describe irritability with youth and caregiver information.
test.interpretation: ARI assesses irritability, not DMDD specifically. The linked parent adaptation is for ages 6–17 and a seven-day interval; it cannot prove the year-long course.

cautions: Use both the child's account and collateral. APA's age rule is more precise than NIMH's simplified 6–10 wording; do not automatically add ODD when DMDD criteria are met.

sources.title: APA: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder fact sheet
NIMH: DMDD — the basics
APA: Parent ARI irritability measure, ages 6–17

name: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder
course: Establish repeated mood and functional changes before menstruation with improvement afterwards; use prospective daily records across at least two menstrual cycles to clarify the pattern.

checklist.label: Relationship to menstruation
checklist.question: Where in your cycle do these changes begin and ease?

checklist.label: Specific emotional changes
checklist.question: What changes in mood, tension or irritability stand out then?

checklist.label: Symptoms outside that phase
checklist.question: How do you feel during the rest of the cycle?

checklist.label: Recurring impact
checklist.question: What becomes difficult at school, work or in relationships during those days?

checklist.label: Daily records and other causes
checklist.question: What daily records, medicines or ongoing mood difficulties help explain the pattern?

test.name: Daily Record of Severity of Problems (DRSP)
test.purpose: Prospectively track symptoms and impairment across menstrual phases.
test.interpretation: The published measure supports clinical assessment; retrospective recall or a single daily score cannot establish PMDD. No DRSP scoring is implemented here.

cautions: Do not infer menstruation from name, gender or life-stage label. The DRSP validation cited used adults and DSM-IV-era definitions; current clinical interpretation remains necessary.

sources.title: APA: Depression and related conditions
Endicott, Nee and Harrison: DRSP reliability and validity (2006; abstract)
Office on Women's Health: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder
NHS: PMDD, diagnosis and prospective symptom diary

name: Bipolar I disorder
course: A manic episode is central: typically at least seven days, or a shorter severe episode requiring hospitalization. Depression may occur but is not required.

checklist.label: Distinct change from usual mood and energy
checklist.question: Describe the clearest period when your energy and behavior were unlike your usual self.

checklist.label: Sleep need and activity
checklist.question: How much sleep did you need, and what were you doing during that time?

checklist.label: Episode duration and recovery
checklist.question: How long did that period last, and what happened afterwards?

checklist.label: Consequences and loss of control
checklist.question: Did it disrupt responsibilities, require hospital care or involve experiences others did not share?

checklist.label: Substances, health and collateral
checklist.question: What medicines or substances were involved, and what did people close to you observe?

differentials: Medical causes such as thyroid illness
Psychotic disorders; compare mood and psychosis chronology

test.name: Specialist longitudinal mood assessment
test.purpose: Reconstruct mania, depression, baseline functioning and collateral accounts.
test.interpretation: Symptom ratings support assessment but cannot independently establish bipolar I. Severe mania or psychosis needs urgent clinical assessment.

cautions: Ordinary mood changes are insufficient. Assess safety, self-care and impaired judgment directly; do not assume dangerousness from the label.

sources.title: NIMH: Bipolar disorder
APA: What are bipolar disorders?

name: Bipolar II disorder
course: Establish both hypomanic and major depressive episodes, without a manic episode; the hypomanic duration anchor is four consecutive days.

checklist.label: Depressive episodes
checklist.question: Which low periods most affected your daily life, and how long did they last?

checklist.label: Distinct increased-energy periods
checklist.question: Were there separate stretches of increased energy that others noticed?

checklist.label: Sleep need and duration
checklist.question: During those stretches, what happened to sleep, and how many days did the change continue?

checklist.label: History of more severe elevation
checklist.question: Has any energized period caused major disruption, hospital care or psychosis?

checklist.label: Baseline and possible causes
checklist.question: How did you function between episodes, and were medicines or substances involved?

differentials: Major depressive disorder with missed hypomania
Bipolar I if mania has occurred
Substance effects or chronic attention difficulties

test.name: Specialist episode-history assessment
test.purpose: Review both depressive and elevated periods with corroborating history.
test.interpretation: No brief depression or mania scale definitively distinguishes bipolar II. A history consistent with mania changes the formulation.

cautions: Hypomania may be remembered as productive, so ask about observable change. Bipolar II can involve severe depression; review safety separately.

sources.title: APA: What are bipolar disorders?
NIMH: Bipolar disorder

name: Cyclothymic disorder
course: Review a fluctuating subthreshold mood pattern across two years in adults or one year in youth; brief diary changes are insufficient.

checklist.label: Recurring energized periods
checklist.question: What do your more energized stretches look like?

checklist.label: Recurring low periods
checklist.question: How are your lower stretches different from your usual mood?

checklist.label: Timeline and gaps
checklist.question: Across the longer history, how long have the better intervals lasted?

checklist.label: Possible full mood episodes
checklist.question: Has any period been severe or sustained enough to cause major disruption or require treatment?

checklist.label: Consequences and other causes
checklist.question: How has the pattern affected relationships or responsibilities, and what else could explain it?

differentials: Bipolar I or II with full episodes

test.name: Longitudinal mood timeline with clinical assessment
test.purpose: Compare symptom periods, gaps, functional effects and full-episode history.
test.interpretation: Mood journals assist assessment but are not a definitive diagnosis; a short observation window cannot establish cyclothymia.

cautions: Do not equate hourly emotional shifts with cyclothymia. Subthreshold symptoms can still impair life; assess safety and changes suggesting a full episode.

sources.title: NHS: Cyclothymia
APA: What are bipolar disorders?

name: Generalized anxiety disorder
course: Explore difficult-to-control worry across several areas on most days for at least six months, with age-appropriate associated features and impairment.

checklist.label: Breadth of worry
checklist.question: What subjects keep coming back in your worries?

checklist.label: Difficulty disengaging
checklist.question: What happens when you try to put the worries aside?

checklist.label: Persistence
checklist.question: When did this pattern start, and how often is it present?

checklist.label: Tension, sleep and concentration
checklist.question: How does worry affect your body, sleep or concentration?

checklist.label: Consequences and alternatives
checklist.question: What does worry stop you doing, and what health or substance changes overlap with it?

differentials: Other anxiety disorders with narrower triggers

test.name: APA Generalized Anxiety Disorder Severity Measure—Adult
test.purpose: Assess recent anxiety burden after symptoms have been identified.
test.interpretation: A severity aid, not a definitive diagnostic test; it cannot establish six-month duration. Use an age-appropriate youth assessment for children.

cautions: Do not apply an adult symptom-count rule to children. Check whether worry concerns actual ongoing danger and obtain caregiver context when appropriate.

sources.title: NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder
APA: Adult generalized anxiety severity measure
AACAP: Anxiety disorder frequently asked questions

name: Panic disorder
course: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks must be distinguished from isolated attacks; examine at least a month of continuing concern or related behavior changes.

checklist.label: Description of an attack
checklist.question: Tell me what happened during the most recent sudden surge of fear.

checklist.label: Unexpected versus cue-linked attacks
checklist.question: Were attacks surprising, or did they occur around a particular fear?

checklist.label: Worry and changed behavior
checklist.question: Since the attacks, what have you worried about or stopped doing?

checklist.label: Recurrence and duration
checklist.question: When did attacks begin, and how long have the changes afterwards continued?

checklist.label: Health and substance review
checklist.question: What medical assessment or medicine and substance changes are relevant?

test.name: APA Panic Disorder Severity Measure—Adult
test.purpose: Describe recent attacks, fear and avoidance as part of assessment.
test.interpretation: Measures symptom burden, not a definitive diagnosis. A raised score does not establish unexpected attacks or exclude medical causes.

cautions: New severe chest symptoms, fainting or breathing difficulty require medical assessment rather than an assumption of panic. Use appropriate youth evaluation for adolescents.

sources.title: NIMH: Panic disorder
APA: Adult panic disorder severity measure

name: Social anxiety disorder
course: Assess persistent fear of negative evaluation with avoidance or marked distress and functional effects, generally across at least six months.

checklist.label: Feared social outcome
checklist.question: What do you fear other people might notice or think?

checklist.label: Situations and breadth
checklist.question: Which social or performance situations are difficult, and which feel comfortable?

checklist.label: Avoidance and endurance
checklist.question: What do you do to get through or avoid those situations?

checklist.label: Persistence and development
checklist.question: When did this pattern begin, including around peers when you were younger?

checklist.label: Lost opportunities and context
checklist.question: How has this affected friendships, learning or work, and are bullying or communication differences involved?

test.name: APA Social Anxiety Disorder Severity Measure—Adult
test.purpose: Describe recent fear, avoidance and interference.
test.interpretation: A severity assessment aid, not a definitive diagnosis. Use developmentally appropriate interviewing or a suitable youth form for children.

cautions: Context and actual discrimination matter. Do not diagnose from quietness alone or assume childhood anxiety only around unfamiliar adults meets the pattern.

sources.title: NIMH: Social anxiety disorder
APA: Adult social anxiety severity measure

name: Specific phobia
course: Explore persistent fear tied to a particular object or situation, generally for six months or more, with distress or interference; distinguish ordinary developmental fear and actual danger.

checklist.label: Specific feared trigger
checklist.question: What particular object or situation brings the fear on?

checklist.label: Response when exposed
checklist.question: What happens in your body and thoughts when it is nearby?

checklist.label: Avoidance
checklist.question: How have you arranged life to avoid it?

checklist.label: Persistence across time
checklist.question: How long has this fear lasted, and has it changed?

checklist.label: Impact and realistic threat
checklist.question: What important activity is affected, and what risk is actually present?

test.name: APA Specific Phobia Severity Measure—Adult
test.purpose: Describe recent fear and avoidance for an identified trigger.
test.interpretation: Severity assessment, not definitive diagnosis; it does not establish the full diagnostic course. Use appropriate child assessment for younger patients.

cautions: Do not provoke exposure during a diagnostic chat. Avoid classifying reasonable caution in dangerous settings as illness.

sources.title: NHS: Phobias
AACAP: Anxiety disorder frequently asked questions
APA: Adult specific phobia severity measure
SAMHSA (2016): DSM-IV to DSM-5 specific-phobia comparison, Table 3.11 (official search extract)

name: Agoraphobia
course: Explore fear across distinct types of situation where escape or help feels difficult; the usual persistence anchor is six months or longer.

checklist.label: Feared difficulty escaping or getting help
checklist.question: What do you fear would happen if you felt unwell away from safety?

checklist.label: Breadth of situations
checklist.question: Which kinds of places are difficult, and how do they differ?

checklist.label: Avoidance and reliance on companions
checklist.question: What changes when someone accompanies you?

checklist.label: Persistent course
checklist.question: When did this begin, and how regularly does it affect outings?

checklist.label: Independence and other explanations
checklist.question: How does this affect daily needs, and are mobility, health or practical barriers involved?

differentials: Physical limitations or realistic environmental barriers

test.name: APA Agoraphobia Severity Measure—Adult
test.purpose: Track recent avoidance, anxiety and dependence on support in feared settings.
test.interpretation: A severity aid, not definitive diagnosis; interview the type and breadth of fears and check other explanations.

cautions: Staying at home alone is not diagnostic. A history of panic disorder is not required; assess the reason for avoidance.

sources.title: APA: What are anxiety disorders?
NHS: Agoraphobia diagnosis
APA: Adult agoraphobia severity measure

name: Separation anxiety disorder
course: Compare separation distress with developmental expectations; public APA guidance gives at least four weeks in youth and typically six months in adults.

checklist.label: Focus of separation fear
checklist.question: Who is difficult to be apart from, and what do you fear might happen?

checklist.label: Anticipated and actual separation
checklist.question: What happens before a separation and once you are apart?

checklist.label: Physical distress and sleeping apart
checklist.question: How does separation affect sleep or physical comfort?

checklist.label: Course and developmental context
checklist.question: How long has this continued, and what recent changes or losses are relevant?

checklist.label: Interference and collateral
checklist.question: What does this prevent you doing, and what do caregivers or school staff observe?

test.name: Structured separation-anxiety assessment; age-appropriate severity aid
test.purpose: Review attachment context, development and functioning. APA provides an adult severity measure.
test.interpretation: The linked adult measure is a severity aid, not a definitive diagnosis and not a preschool test; young children need caregiver-informed assessment.

cautions: Do not pathologize typical toddler distress or assume school refusal has only one explanation.

sources.title: APA: What are anxiety disorders?
AACAP: Anxiety disorder frequently asked questions
NIMH: Children and mental health — assessment
APA: Adult separation anxiety severity measure

name: Selective mutism
course: Establish at least a month of a setting-dependent speaking difficulty beyond the initial school adjustment month, despite speech in other settings.

checklist.label: Where speech is available
checklist.question: Where and with whom is speaking comfortable, and where does it become difficult?

checklist.label: Onset and persistence
checklist.question: When was the difference first noticed, and has it persisted beyond settling into school?

checklist.label: Other ways of communicating
checklist.question: Would pointing, writing or another way of responding feel easier here?

checklist.label: Language and hearing context
checklist.question: How is communication in each familiar language, and what hearing or language assessment exists?

checklist.label: Participation and corroboration
checklist.question: How does this affect learning or friendships, and what do caregivers and teachers notice?

test.name: Interdisciplinary speech-language and mental-health assessment
test.purpose: Compare communication across settings with caregiver, teacher and direct observations.
test.interpretation: Screening guides further assessment; a text conversation cannot definitively establish selective mutism or measure spoken performance.

cautions: Do not pressure speech or treat silence as deliberate defiance. Permit nonverbal responses and distinguish language proficiency from anxiety.

sources.title: ASHA Practice Portal: Selective mutism
NHS: Selective mutism

name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
course: Investigate recurring unwanted intrusions and/or driven rituals that consume time or cause distress/impairment; there is no universal six-month requirement.

checklist.label: Unwanted intrusive experiences
checklist.question: Are there thoughts or images that arrive against your wishes and keep troubling you?

checklist.label: Overt and mental rituals
checklist.question: What do you feel driven to do or repeat in your mind afterwards?

checklist.label: Purpose and temporary relief
checklist.question: What do you hope the ritual will prevent, and how long does relief last?

checklist.label: Time, avoidance and interference
checklist.question: How much of your day does this take, and what gets pushed aside?

checklist.label: Insight and context
checklist.question: How do you understand these experiences, and how are they different from your usual preferences?

test.name: APA repetitive thoughts/behaviors measure (adapted FOCI severity scale)
test.purpose: Describe adult obsessive-compulsive symptom burden.
test.interpretation: A severity aid, not a definitive OCD diagnosis. Youth need an appropriate version and caregiver context; no questionnaire is reproduced here.

cautions: Unwanted harm thoughts are not the same as intent. Assess safety by direct inquiry without treating obsession content as proof of dangerousness.

sources.title: NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
APA: Adult repetitive thoughts/behaviors measure, adapted FOCI severity scale

name: Body dysmorphic disorder
course: Explore persistent appearance preoccupation, repetitive responses and impairment; do not infer the disorder from an appearance concern alone.

checklist.label: Meaning of appearance concerns
checklist.question: What concerns about your appearance occupy your attention?

checklist.label: Time and control
checklist.question: How much time do these concerns take, and can you shift attention away?

checklist.label: Checking, comparison or concealment
checklist.question: What do you find yourself doing in response to the concern?

checklist.label: Avoidance and distress
checklist.question: What have you missed or avoided because of it?

checklist.label: Eating concerns, insight and safety
checklist.question: How does this connect with eating or weight concerns, and has the distress affected your safety?

test.name: Body Dysmorphic Disorder Questionnaire (BDDQ)
test.purpose: Identify a possible BDD presentation that merits a clinical interview.
test.interpretation: A screening tool, not a definitive diagnosis. Confirm with appropriate interview; BDD-YBOCS is a separate severity tool, not a screening substitute.

cautions: Avoid repeatedly reassuring or judging appearance. Check suicide/self-harm concerns and whether eating pathology better explains the concern.

sources.title: IOCDF / Katharine Phillips: Clinical assessment of BDD
IOCDF: Assessment tools for BDD

name: Hoarding disorder
course: Assess persistent difficulty discarding and accumulation over time; the state of a room on one day may reflect others having cleared it.

checklist.label: Difficulty parting with possessions
checklist.question: What happens when you consider letting an item go?

checklist.label: Perceived need to keep items
checklist.question: What would losing or discarding it mean to you?

checklist.label: Use of living areas
checklist.question: How are rooms used now, and what activities are difficult there?

checklist.label: Accumulation and outside help
checklist.question: How did the situation develop, and has anyone else cleared or managed things?

checklist.label: Functioning and household safety
checklist.question: How does this affect relationships, daily tasks or moving safely through the home?

differentials: Other disorders causing accumulation or self-neglect

test.name: Hoarding Rating Scale–Interview (HRS-I)
test.purpose: Assess clutter, discarding, acquisition, distress and functional burden.
test.interpretation: A structured assessment aid; scores suggest severity or concern, not a definitive diagnosis without context and differential assessment.

cautions: Assess fire and access hazards sensitively. Do not infer hoarding from poverty, clutter alone or a photograph, or treat forced clearing as an assessment.

sources.title: APA: What is hoarding disorder?
Tolin et al.: Development and validation of the Hoarding Rating Scale–Interview
IOCDF: Clinical assessment of hoarding

name: Trichotillomania (hair-pulling disorder)
course: Map onset and recurring pulling; often begins around puberty. There is no arbitrary simulated-day threshold.

checklist.label: Pulling and hair loss
checklist.question: What have you noticed happening to your hair?

checklist.label: Awareness and situations
checklist.question: When are you most likely to notice yourself pulling?

checklist.label: Efforts to stop
checklist.question: What has happened when you tried to reduce it?

checklist.label: Distress and participation
checklist.question: Has this changed where you go or what you feel comfortable doing?

checklist.label: Skin conditions and appearance motives
checklist.question: What else seems connected to it, and has anyone checked your scalp?

differentials: Appearance-driven removal in body dysmorphic disorder

test.name: MGH Hairpulling Scale
test.purpose: Measures pulling severity and perceived control.
test.interpretation: A severity assessment, not a standalone diagnosis. The cited development study concerns adults; do not assume the same measurement properties in children or adolescents.

cautions: Avoid assuming intent to self-harm. Medical examination remains relevant to hair loss.

sources.title: APA: Obsessive-compulsive and related disorders
Keuthen et al. (1995): MGH Hairpulling Scale development

name: Excoriation (skin-picking) disorder
course: Establish a recurring course and attempts to stop, rather than diagnosing isolated picking.

checklist.label: Picking and skin damage
checklist.question: What changes have you noticed in your skin?

checklist.label: Urges or automatic picking
checklist.question: What is usually happening when you start noticing the picking?

checklist.label: Efforts to reduce
checklist.question: What have you tried, and what happened?

checklist.label: Avoidance and disruption
checklist.question: Has this affected clothing choices, activities, or seeing people?

checklist.label: Medical and alternative explanations
checklist.question: What skin problems, medicines, or other changes came before this?

differentials: Appearance-focused picking in body dysmorphic disorder

test.name: Skin Picking Scale (SPS)
test.purpose: Assesses the severity of repetitive skin picking.
test.interpretation: Severity information supports clinical assessment; it does not establish the cause or a diagnosis.

cautions: Do not treat lesions as proof of psychiatric illness. Wounds with infection or significant bleeding need medical assessment.

sources.title: APA: Obsessive-compulsive and related disorders
Keuthen et al. (2001): Skin Picking Scale development

name: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
course: Document qualifying trauma and symptoms lasting longer than one month; recent simulated days cannot supply an absent earlier history.

checklist.label: Exposure and timeline
checklist.question: Without details you do not want to discuss, what happened and when did these changes begin?

checklist.label: Unwanted reliving
checklist.question: Do reminders bring back the experience when you do not want them to?

checklist.label: Avoidance
checklist.question: What have you found yourself steering away from since then?

checklist.label: Mood, beliefs and alertness
checklist.question: How have your sense of safety, mood, sleep, or reactions changed?

checklist.label: Functioning and current safety
checklist.question: What is hardest to manage now, and are you safe where you are?

test.name: PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5)
test.purpose: Adult symptom screening and monitoring.
test.interpretation: A provisional screen; a clinician-administered interview such as CAPS-5 assesses diagnosis. Use youth-appropriate assessment for adolescents.

cautions: Do not demand graphic trauma details. Exposure, duration, impairment and alternatives require separate evidence.

sources.title: APA: PTSD and related conditions
VA National Center for PTSD: PCL-5

name: Acute stress disorder
course: The acute-stress window is 3 days to 1 month after a qualifying trauma; later PTSD is not inevitable.

checklist.label: Exposure and exact timing
checklist.question: When did the event occur, and when did these changes start?

checklist.label: Unwanted memories or dreams
checklist.question: What happens when memories of the event come up?

checklist.label: Detachment and mood
checklist.question: Have you felt distant from yourself or your surroundings since then?

checklist.label: Avoidance and alertness
checklist.question: What are you avoiding, and how easy is it to rest or feel safe?

checklist.label: Impairment and immediate needs
checklist.question: What support or practical help do you need to get through today?

test.name: Acute Stress Disorder Structured Interview-5 (ASDI-5)
test.purpose: Trained-clinician assessment of the acute presentation.
test.interpretation: The VA notes limited validation of DSM-5 updates; this is not a self-scored definitive test. For children or adolescents, a trained clinician must select a developmentally appropriate assessment.

cautions: Address physical injury and present safety. Do not turn early distress into a prediction of chronic illness.

sources.title: VA National Center for PTSD: Acute stress disorder

name: Adjustment disorders
course: Relate onset to a stressor within 3 months. Symptoms ordinarily resolve within 6 months after its consequences end.

checklist.label: Identifiable change
checklist.question: What changed in your life before this became difficult?

checklist.label: Stressor-symptom sequence
checklist.question: How soon after that change did you notice a difference?

checklist.label: Emotional or behavioral response
checklist.question: How have you been reacting, in your own words?

checklist.label: Impact and cultural context
checklist.question: What has become harder, and how do people important to you understand this situation?

checklist.label: Broader history and recovery
checklist.question: Was anything similar happening before, and what has improved or persisted?

test.name: Structured stressor and functioning assessment
test.purpose: Organizes stressor timing, impact and competing explanations.
test.interpretation: This clinical assessment has no standalone pass score; the proposed formulation needs contextual judgment.

cautions: A stressful event does not itself establish illness. A continuing stressor can extend the course.

sources.title: APA: PTSD and related conditions

name: Prolonged grief disorder
course: DSM-5-TR timing: bereavement at least 12 months earlier in adults, or 6 months in children/adolescents; consider cultural expectations.

checklist.label: Loss and chronology
checklist.question: Who did you lose, and how long ago was the loss?

checklist.label: Longing and preoccupation
checklist.question: How much of your day is taken up by missing or thinking about them?

checklist.label: Identity and meaning
checklist.question: How has the loss changed your sense of who you are or what matters?

checklist.label: Rejoining everyday life
checklist.question: Which relationships or activities remain difficult to return to?

checklist.label: Culture, support and safety
checklist.question: What does mourning mean in your family, and what support do you have when things feel unbearable?

test.name: Structured bereavement assessment
test.purpose: Examines persistent grief, functioning and the cultural setting.
test.interpretation: Assessment supports a clinical formulation; elapsed time or sadness alone is not a diagnostic test.

cautions: Do not pathologize continuing love or remembrance. Ask about safety without assuming suicidal intent.

sources.title: APA: Prolonged grief disorder

name: Reactive attachment disorder
course: Assess early developmental and caregiving history; RAD difficulties emerge before age 5, rather than arising from a recent simulated week.

checklist.label: Seeking comfort from a caregiver
checklist.question: When the child is upset, whom do they approach?

checklist.label: Response to comfort
checklist.question: What happens when a familiar caregiver tries to soothe them?

checklist.label: Emotion during familiar contact
checklist.question: What are ordinary play and quiet time together like?

checklist.label: Documented care history
checklist.question: Who has cared for the child over time, and what records can clarify that history?

checklist.label: Development and observations
checklist.question: How does this differ across familiar people, and what developmental assessments are available?

test.name: Specialist developmental and caregiver assessment
test.purpose: Combines observation, caregiver accounts and care records.
test.interpretation: Attachment-style measures alone do not diagnose RAD; a qualified assessment must examine the diagnostic requirements.

cautions: Use caregiver interview and observation for young children. Do not infer neglect from withdrawal or from placement status.

sources.title: AACAP: Attachment disorders
APA: PTSD and related conditions
NICE NG26: Children's attachment, assessment recommendations

name: Disinhibited social engagement disorder
course: Establish early insufficient-care history and a persistent developmentally unusual social pattern; a single friendly encounter is insufficient.

checklist.label: Boundaries with unfamiliar adults
checklist.question: What happens when the child meets an adult they do not know?

checklist.label: Checking back with caregivers
checklist.question: In a new place, how does the child keep track of their caregiver?

checklist.label: Willingness to leave safely
checklist.question: Have there been times the child went with someone unfamiliar?

checklist.label: Caregiving history
checklist.question: What reliable information is available about early care and caregiver changes?

checklist.label: Development and consequences
checklist.question: How does this compare with peers, and what concerns arise across settings?

test.name: Specialist developmental and caregiver assessment
test.purpose: Examines social boundaries, early care and observed functioning.
test.interpretation: This is a clinical assessment, not a personality quiz; no one checklist confirms DSED.

cautions: Prioritize child safety without staging risky stranger encounters. Care history must be documented, not guessed.

sources.title: AACAP: Attachment disorders
NICE NG26: Children's attachment, assessment recommendations
APA: PTSD and related conditions

name: Depersonalization/derealization disorder
course: Clarify recurrent or persistent detachment and its impact; episodes have no universal short duration threshold.

checklist.label: Type of detachment
checklist.question: How would you describe the strange or distant feeling?

checklist.label: Understanding during episodes
checklist.question: While it happens, what do you believe about whether things are actually unreal?

checklist.label: Onset and recurrence
checklist.question: When did it first happen, and how does an episode unfold?

checklist.label: Distress and functioning
checklist.question: What becomes difficult while this feeling is present?

checklist.label: Panic, substances and physical events
checklist.question: What else is happening around the episodes, including sleep, medicines or illness?

test.name: Structured dissociation and medical assessment
test.purpose: Separates subjective detachment from altered reality testing and medical causes.
test.interpretation: An assessment pathway, not a self-scoring diagnostic test.

cautions: Preserved recognition of the experience as a feeling is a key distinction; sudden atypical symptoms need medical review.

sources.title: APA: Dissociative disorders
NHS: Dissociative disorders

name: Dissociative amnesia
course: Describe the boundaries and timing of autobiographical memory gaps; ordinary forgetfulness is different.

checklist.label: Specific missing memories
checklist.question: Which periods or personal information are difficult to recall?

checklist.label: What remains remembered
checklist.question: What do you remember clearly around that time?

checklist.label: Onset and discovery
checklist.question: When did you first notice the gap, and how did you notice it?

checklist.label: Practical consequences
checklist.question: How has this affected your daily tasks or relationships?

checklist.label: Alternative causes and corroboration
checklist.question: Were there injuries, illness, substances, or records that might help clarify what happened?

test.name: Structured memory-history and medical assessment
test.purpose: Clarifies autobiographical gaps and possible physical explanations.
test.interpretation: Clinical assessment is needed; the checklist neither verifies past events nor diagnoses amnesia.

cautions: Use neutral questions. Do not suggest hidden trauma or fill gaps with recovered-memory narratives.

sources.title: APA: Dissociative disorders
NHS: Dissociative disorders

name: Dissociative identity disorder
course: Assess identity discontinuity and recurrent memory gaps over time; changes in mood or preferences alone are insufficient.

checklist.label: Sense of self and agency
checklist.question: Have there been times your actions or sense of self felt unexpectedly unfamiliar?

checklist.label: Everyday memory gaps
checklist.question: Have you found evidence of ordinary activities you cannot remember doing?

checklist.label: Recurring pattern
checklist.question: How long has this been happening, and who has noticed changes?

checklist.label: Functioning and safety
checklist.question: What problems does this create for you in daily life?

checklist.label: Culture and alternative explanations
checklist.question: How do you understand these experiences, including any cultural practices, medical conditions or substances?

differentials: Psychotic symptoms or culturally accepted experiences

test.name: Specialist structured dissociation assessment
test.purpose: Evaluates identity, memory and competing explanations together.
test.interpretation: A specialist assessment, not an online test or confirmation from apparent switching.

cautions: Do not invite theatrical switching, invent separate biographies, or assume abuse. Ask about current safety respectfully.

sources.title: APA: Dissociative disorders
NHS: Dissociative disorders

name: Somatic symptom disorder
course: Establish a persistent symptomatic course, typically beyond 6 months; the individual physical symptom may change during that period.

checklist.label: Physical experience
checklist.question: What physical symptoms are most difficult for you?

checklist.label: Thoughts about symptoms
checklist.question: What do those symptoms make you fear or expect?

checklist.label: Time and energy devoted to health
checklist.question: How does managing or thinking about symptoms affect an ordinary day?

checklist.label: Course and functional changes
checklist.question: When did this pattern begin, and what have you stopped doing?

checklist.label: Medical findings and new changes
checklist.question: What has been assessed medically, and is anything new or worsening?

differentials: Illness anxiety with little symptom burden
Depression or anxiety with physical symptoms

test.name: Structured physical-symptom and health-concern assessment
test.purpose: Reviews symptom burden, beliefs, behavior and medical findings.
test.interpretation: A clinical assessment; normal investigations or a symptom count do not diagnose this disorder.

cautions: Symptoms are real. Coexisting medical illness is possible; new red flags require evaluation.

sources.title: APA: Somatic symptom disorder
SAMHSA (2016): DSM-5 somatic symptom comparison

name: Illness anxiety disorder
course: Establish health preoccupation for at least 6 months; the feared illness can change during that time.

checklist.label: Feared illness
checklist.question: What illness worries you most, and what makes it feel likely?

checklist.label: Symptoms versus fear
checklist.question: How much difficulty comes from physical symptoms compared with fear about what they mean?

checklist.label: Checking or reassurance
checklist.question: What do you do when the concern appears, and how long does reassurance help?

checklist.label: Avoiding health information or care
checklist.question: Are there appointments or activities you avoid because of these fears?

checklist.label: Course and disruption
checklist.question: How long has this occupied your life, and what has it interrupted?

differentials: Appropriate concern about a medical problem

test.name: Structured health-anxiety assessment
test.purpose: Explores feared illness, checking, avoidance and functioning.
test.interpretation: This assessment supports further evaluation; health anxiety is not confirmed by one reassuring test.

cautions: Do not dismiss emerging physical symptoms. NHS health-anxiety guidance is broader than a complete DSM diagnosis.

sources.title: APA: Somatic symptom and illness anxiety expert questions
NHS: Health anxiety
SAMHSA (2016): DSM-5 illness anxiety comparison

name: Functional neurological symptom disorder (conversion disorder)
course: Record onset, recurrence and change in motor or sensory symptoms; a psychological stressor is not necessary to establish the condition.

checklist.label: Neurological symptom description
checklist.question: What happens during the weakness, altered sensation, movement, or episodes?

checklist.label: Onset and variation
checklist.question: When did this begin, and how does it vary through the day?

checklist.label: Daily functioning
checklist.question: Which activities are affected and what support do you need?

checklist.label: Existing neurological findings
checklist.question: What did the neurologist find and explain during your examination?

checklist.label: Coexisting illness and new symptoms
checklist.question: Have you been told about another neurological condition, or noticed a new change?

differentials: Other medical causes of motor or sensory changes

test.name: Neurological history and examination for positive functional signs
test.purpose: A clinician examines signs appropriate to the specific presentation.
test.interpretation: This assessment cannot be performed by chat. Normal scans or a trauma history alone do not confirm FND.

cautions: New acute neurological deficits need urgent medical evaluation. Functional and other neurological disorders can coexist.

sources.title: King's College Hospital NHS: Functional neurological disorder

name: Anorexia nervosa
course: Review restrictive intake over time alongside the person's growth or weight trajectory and developmental context; appearance is insufficient.

checklist.label: Restrictive eating pattern
checklist.question: How has eating changed for you over time?

checklist.label: Concerns about weight gain
checklist.question: What feels most difficult about eating more or changes in your body?

checklist.label: Body image and self-worth
checklist.question: How much does body shape or weight affect how you judge yourself?

checklist.label: Physical changes and clinical assessment
checklist.question: What physical changes have you noticed, and what has your clinician checked?

checklist.label: Participation and support
checklist.question: How has eating affected school, work, relationships, or shared meals?

differentials: ARFID without weight or shape motives
Medical causes of reduced intake or weight loss
Atypical anorexia or other eating disorders

test.name: Comprehensive eating-disorder and medical assessment
test.purpose: Combines eating history, physical health and developmental growth records.
test.interpretation: A screening questionnaire alone cannot diagnose anorexia; clinical assessment and medical risk review are needed.

cautions: Medical instability can be urgent. Do not infer health from body size or introduce calorie or weight-loss targets.

sources.title: NIMH: Eating disorders, what you need to know
NICE NG69: Eating disorders, identification and assessment

name: Bulimia nervosa
course: Establish binge eating and compensatory behavior averaging at least weekly for 3 months, alongside the broader eating history.

checklist.label: Episode and loss of control
checklist.question: Can you describe what an episode of eating that feels out of control is like?

checklist.label: Responses after eating
checklist.question: What tends to happen afterward when you worry about the eating?

checklist.label: Frequency and persistence
checklist.question: How often does this cycle happen, and how long has it been going on?

checklist.label: Weight or shape in self-evaluation
checklist.question: How do concerns about your body affect how you feel about yourself?

checklist.label: Health and life impact
checklist.question: Have you felt faint, physically unwell, or had trouble keeping up with daily life?

test.name: Comprehensive eating-disorder and medical assessment
test.purpose: Examines binge episodes, compensatory patterns and physical risk.
test.interpretation: An assessment rather than a standalone screening diagnosis; frequency and full exclusions need clinician review.

cautions: Purging can cause serious medical complications at any body size. Ask without procedural details.

sources.title: APA: Eating disorders
NIMH: Eating disorders, what you need to know
NICE NG69: Eating disorders, identification and assessment
Mayo Clinic: Bulimia diagnosis and treatment

name: Binge-eating disorder
course: A diagnostic timing anchor is recurring binge episodes at least weekly for 3 months; impact and the broader eating pattern also matter.

checklist.label: Episode and loss of control
checklist.question: What happens during the times eating feels difficult to control?

checklist.label: Eating context and associated experience
checklist.question: How does an episode differ from an ordinary meal for you?

checklist.label: Distress about episodes
checklist.question: How do you feel afterward, and what concerns you most?

checklist.label: Frequency and course
checklist.question: How often has this happened over the past few months?

checklist.label: Compensatory pattern and impact
checklist.question: Do you try to undo the eating afterward, and how is this affecting daily life?

test.name: Comprehensive eating-pattern assessment
test.purpose: Clarifies episodes, distress and whether compensation occurs.
test.interpretation: This is a clinical assessment; food quantity or body size alone does not diagnose binge-eating disorder.

cautions: Avoid moral judgments and weight-loss advice. Lower-frequency symptoms can still warrant care.

sources.title: APA: Eating disorders
NIMH: Eating disorders, what you need to know

name: Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID)
course: Review feeding development and an ongoing restrictive pattern; substantial social interference can matter even without low weight.

checklist.label: Foods and intake affected
checklist.question: What makes eating certain foods or enough food difficult?

checklist.label: Sensory, appetite or feared-consequence drivers
checklist.question: Is it the sensation, little interest in eating, fear of something happening, or something else?

checklist.label: Nutrition, growth and participation
checklist.question: How has this affected health, growth, energy, or eating with others?

checklist.label: Weight and shape concerns
checklist.question: Are concerns about body shape or weight part of why eating is difficult?

checklist.label: Access, culture and feeding skills
checklist.question: What foods are available, and have swallowing, digestion, or feeding skills been checked?

test.name: Pica, ARFID and Rumination Disorder Interview (PARDI)
test.purpose: A specialist multi-informant assessment of feeding presentations.
test.interpretation: The initial pilot involved ages 10–22; use an age-appropriate version and multidisciplinary assessment for younger children. It is not a chat-based diagnostic test.

cautions: Use caregiver observations for toddlers. Do not assume sensory selectivity alone is ARFID.

sources.title: Bryant-Waugh et al. (2019): PARDI development
APA DSM-5-TR: ARFID clarification
NIMH: Eating disorders, what you need to know

name: Enuresis
course: Review toileting development, repeated wetting and previous dry periods; ordinary toddler accidents are not the target.

checklist.label: Daytime versus nighttime wetting
checklist.question: When does wetting happen, and how often?

checklist.label: Toileting and previous dryness
checklist.question: How did toilet learning go, and was there a long period without accidents?

checklist.label: Associated physical symptoms
checklist.question: Has there been pain, urgency, unusual thirst, or a change in urine?

checklist.label: Bowel and sleep history
checklist.question: What are bowel movements and sleep like?

checklist.label: Child's experience and support
checklist.question: How is this affecting you, and how do others respond when it happens?

differentials: Urinary tract or other medical problems

test.name: Bladder diary with pediatric medical assessment
test.purpose: Records wetting and voiding patterns; clinicians decide examination and urine testing.
test.interpretation: A diary aids assessment, not a standalone psychiatric diagnosis.

cautions: Involve the child without blame and obtain caregiver history. New wetting or physical symptoms needs medical review.

sources.title: AACAP: Bedwetting
NIDDK: Diagnosing bladder control problems in children

name: Encopresis
course: Review bowel-control development, recurrence and earlier continence; preschool developmental expectations and medical causes must be considered.

checklist.label: Soiling pattern
checklist.question: When does stool get onto clothes or somewhere unexpected?

checklist.label: Constipation and overflow possibility
checklist.question: Do bowel movements hurt or feel difficult, or are there long gaps between them?

checklist.label: Toileting history and access
checklist.question: What has toilet learning been like, and is there a comfortable toilet available?

checklist.label: Medical and medication history
checklist.question: What has been checked medically, and what medicines are being taken?

checklist.label: Emotional and practical consequences
checklist.question: How does this affect school or seeing friends, and what help feels useful?

test.name: Bowel diary with pediatric assessment
test.purpose: Clarifies stool patterns, withholding, physical findings and contributing illness.
test.interpretation: Clinical assessment is required; a diary or interview alone cannot diagnose or exclude bowel disease.

cautions: Avoid blame or interpreting soiling as defiance. Address pain, medical red flags and accessibility.

sources.title: AACAP: Encopresis and bowel control
NIDDK: Diagnosing constipation in children

name: Insomnia disorder
course: Chronic insomnia involves difficulty at least 3 nights weekly for at least 3 months, with daytime impact; establish adequate opportunity for sleep.

checklist.label: Type of sleep difficulty
checklist.question: What happens between going to bed and getting up?

checklist.label: Opportunity and schedule
checklist.question: What time and conditions are available for sleep on workdays and days off?

checklist.label: Frequency and total course
checklist.question: How many nights are difficult, and when did this pattern begin?

checklist.label: Daytime consequences
checklist.question: How does your sleep affect the following day?

checklist.label: Other sleep or medical contributors
checklist.question: Do snoring, breathing, pain, medicines, caffeine, or unusual energy seem involved?

differentials: Mood episodes, substances or medical illness

test.name: Insomnia Severity Index (ISI)
test.purpose: Adult screening and severity monitoring.
test.interpretation: A symptom screen, not a diagnosis; a recent two-week score does not establish the three-month course.

cautions: A short diary samples sleep; it does not replace the longer history. Markedly reduced need for sleep differs from wanting but being unable to sleep.

sources.title: NHLBI: Insomnia diagnosis
VA MIRECC: Insomnia Severity Index screening

name: Oppositional defiant disorder
course: Review a developmentally unusual pattern lasting at least 6 months; isolated conflict is insufficient.

checklist.label: Irritability and recovery
checklist.question: What tends to happen when you feel frustrated, and how do you settle afterward?

checklist.label: Argumentative interactions
checklist.question: Can you walk me through a disagreement from your point of view?

checklist.label: Settings and developmental expectations
checklist.question: With whom does this happen, and are there settings where things go differently?

checklist.label: Effect on daily life
checklist.question: How does this affect learning, friendships, or life at home?

checklist.label: Needs and other explanations
checklist.question: Are worry, communication, attention, sleep, or feeling unsafe making things harder?

test.name: Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) with multi-informant assessment
test.purpose: Broad child behavioral screening using appropriate parent, teacher and youth forms.
test.interpretation: Screening supports assessment; a conduct-subscale score does not diagnose ODD or explain the behavior.

cautions: Hear the child's perspective; use age-appropriate forms and caregiver/teacher information. Do not infer poor character.

sources.title: AACAP: Oppositional defiant disorder
NICE CG158: Conduct disorders, initial and comprehensive assessment
Youthinmind: Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire
AACAP: ODD guide for families (2009)

name: Conduct disorder
course: Review the past 12 months, with behavior also present in the past 6 months; establish developmental onset and impairment.

checklist.label: Specific serious behavioral events
checklist.question: What has happened that brought you here, from your perspective?

checklist.label: Recurrence and age at onset
checklist.question: When did similar problems first happen, and what has happened recently?

checklist.label: Triggers, coercion and context
checklist.question: What was going on around you before and after these events?

checklist.label: Consequences and present safety
checklist.question: Who has been affected, and is anyone at risk now?

checklist.label: Multiple viewpoints and other needs
checklist.question: What would caregivers or teachers add, and are there learning, mood or substance concerns?

test.name: SDQ followed by comprehensive developmental assessment
test.purpose: Initial broad screening plus youth, caregiver and school history.
test.interpretation: The questionnaire does not establish conduct disorder or predict an individual's future violence.

cautions: Do not fabricate offenses, equate diagnosis with criminality, or infer lack of remorse from one exchange.

sources.title: AACAP: Conduct disorder
NICE CG158: Conduct disorders, initial and comprehensive assessment
Youthinmind: Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire
SAMHSA (2016): DSM-5 conduct disorder comparison

name: Alcohol use disorder
course: Review the past 12 months and earlier drinking history; a 28-day diary cannot replace that history.

checklist.label: Pattern and intended limits
checklist.question: How does drinking fit into a usual week, and when does it go beyond what you planned?

checklist.label: Craving and attempts to change
checklist.question: What happens when you decide to drink less?

checklist.label: Consequences and priorities
checklist.question: Which responsibilities or relationships have changed around drinking?

checklist.label: Last drink and withdrawal history
checklist.question: When was your last drink, and what has happened when you stopped before?

checklist.label: Mood, other substances and safety
checklist.question: What else are you taking, and how do your mood and safety change with alcohol?

differentials: Risky drinking without established use disorder
Mood or anxiety symptoms with an independent or alcohol-related course

test.name: AUDIT-C
test.purpose: Brief adult screen for unhealthy drinking, followed by assessment of alcohol-use symptoms.
test.interpretation: A positive screen calls for further evaluation; it does not establish alcohol use disorder. Youth require an age-appropriate approach.

cautions: Seizures, marked confusion or severe withdrawal require urgent medical assessment. Do not simulate advice to stop heavy prolonged drinking abruptly or infer a disorder from quantity alone.

sources.title: NIAAA — Alcohol use disorder: from risk to diagnosis to recovery
NIAAA — Screen and assess: use quick, effective methods

name: Cannabis use disorder
course: Review use and consequences over the past 12 months; separate the longer pattern from effects during use or after cutting down.

checklist.label: Products, frequency and change
checklist.question: What cannabis products do you use, and how has that changed?

checklist.label: Control and craving
checklist.question: What happens when you try to delay or reduce cannabis?

checklist.label: Activities and functioning
checklist.question: Has using cannabis changed school, work, relationships or activities you value?

checklist.label: Timing of mental and sleep changes
checklist.question: How do anxiety, sleep or unusual experiences relate to using or stopping?

checklist.label: Hazardous situations and co-use
checklist.question: Have there been situations where cannabis or other substances made staying safe harder?

differentials: Independent anxiety, psychotic or sleep condition

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag cannabis-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Youth need confidential, developmentally appropriate assessment. Cannabis exposure alone is not a diagnosis; do not assume it explains every mood or perceptual symptom.

sources.title: CDC — Understanding your risk for cannabis use disorder
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening
APA — What is a substance use disorder?

name: Opioid use disorder
course: Assess problematic behavior within the past-year window, including prescribed and nonprescribed exposure.

checklist.label: Pain treatment and source
checklist.question: What are you taking for pain or other reasons, and how does actual use compare with the plan?

checklist.label: Control over use
checklist.question: What happens when you intend to take less or wait longer?

checklist.label: Time and consequences
checklist.question: How much of your day is shaped by getting, using or recovering from opioids?

checklist.label: Supervised dependence versus disorder
checklist.question: Which effects appeared during prescribed treatment, and what other problems occurred?

checklist.label: Overdose and sedative co-use
checklist.question: Have there been episodes of being hard to wake, and what other medicines or substances were involved?

differentials: Physical dependence during appropriate medical treatment
Undertreated pain or another substance-use condition

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag opioid-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Tolerance and withdrawal during solely appropriate medical supervision do not by themselves count toward opioid use disorder. Slow breathing or reduced consciousness is an emergency; do not offer dose or detox instructions.

sources.title: CDC — Opioid use disorder: diagnosis
CDC — Save a life from prescription opioid overdose
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening

name: Stimulant use disorder
course: Map use, impaired control and consequences over the past 12 months, including periods before use and during recovery.

checklist.label: Stimulant and treatment context
checklist.question: Which stimulants are involved, and which are prescribed?

checklist.label: Craving and limits
checklist.question: When have you used differently from what you planned?

checklist.label: Use, sleep and recovery cycle
checklist.question: How do sleep, energy and mood change while using and afterward?

checklist.label: Daily functioning
checklist.question: What has happened to work, school or relationships around this pattern?

checklist.label: Physical and mental warning signs
checklist.question: Have there been chest symptoms, overheating, confusion or frightening perceptions?

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag stimulant-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Chest pain, severe overheating, seizure or marked confusion calls for urgent medical assessment. A prescription for ADHD does not establish a use disorder.

sources.title: CDC — Stimulants
APA — What is a substance use disorder?
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening

name: Sedative, hypnotic, or anxiolytic use disorder
course: Review the past 12 months, including the original prescription, subsequent use pattern and timing of dose reductions or interruptions.

checklist.label: Medication and actual use
checklist.question: Which sleep or anxiety medicines do you take, and how does your use compare with the prescription?

checklist.label: Control and attempts to change
checklist.question: What has happened when you tried to follow a lower amount or reduce use?

checklist.label: Function and adverse consequences
checklist.question: Have memory, alertness, falls or responsibilities changed?

checklist.label: Withdrawal and interruption
checklist.question: What happened when a supply ran out or a dose changed?

checklist.label: Alcohol and opioid combination
checklist.question: What other medicines, alcohol or drugs do you sometimes take at the same time?

differentials: Expected physical dependence during prescribed treatment

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag sedative-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Physical dependence is not synonymous with addiction. Abrupt benzodiazepine reduction may cause life-threatening withdrawal; seizures or severe confusion need urgent medical care. No taper schedules are supplied.

sources.title: FDA — Benzodiazepine boxed warning, dependence and withdrawal
APA — What is a substance use disorder?
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening

name: Tobacco use disorder
course: Review nicotine use, changes and quit attempts over the past 12 months; distinguish withdrawal symptoms from baseline anxiety or poor concentration.

checklist.label: Nicotine products and routines
checklist.question: Which tobacco or nicotine products are part of your day?

checklist.label: Urges and triggers
checklist.question: When are urges hardest to manage?

checklist.label: Attempts to reduce
checklist.question: What happened the last time you tried to cut down or stop?

checklist.label: Symptoms when use is delayed
checklist.question: What changes in sleep, mood or concentration appear when you cannot use nicotine?

checklist.label: Consequences and personal priorities
checklist.question: How has nicotine affected your health, spending or activities you care about?

test.name: TAPS (adult substance-use screen)
test.purpose: Flag tobacco/nicotine-use concerns for a clinical follow-up.
test.interpretation: Screening result only; use age-appropriate assessment for adolescents. The simulation does not administer or score TAPS.

cautions: Include vaping and smokeless products; quantity alone is insufficient. Adult screening guidance should not be copied uncritically to children or adolescents.

sources.title: CDC — Why quitting smoking is hard
NIDA — Tobacco, Alcohol, Prescription Medication, and Other Substance Use Screening

name: Gambling disorder
course: Explore a recurrent past-year pattern, with separate assessment of gambling limited to a manic episode.

checklist.label: Time, money and control
checklist.question: What does a typical gambling session look like, and how often does it exceed your plan?

checklist.label: Response to losses
checklist.question: What tends to happen after a loss?

checklist.label: Financial and relationship harm
checklist.question: What bills, relationships or responsibilities have been affected?

checklist.label: Concealment and support
checklist.question: How easy is it to talk about gambling and seek support?

checklist.label: Mood course and immediate safety
checklist.question: Does gambling change during unusually energized periods, and have losses left you feeling unsafe?

differentials: Other addictive behavior or substance use

test.name: Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI)
test.purpose: Structure discussion of gambling-related harm.
test.interpretation: A harm screen, not a stand-alone DSM diagnosis. This app does not administer its items or calculate its score.

cautions: Assess distress, self-harm risk and affected dependents without moral judgment. Financial loss alone does not establish the disorder.

sources.title: APA — What is gambling disorder?
NICE NG248 — Gambling-related harms: recommendations

name: Schizophrenia
course: Establish at least six months of overall disturbance, with the active symptom period and treatment-related exceptions assessed separately.

checklist.label: Perception and beliefs
checklist.question: What experiences have felt unusual or difficult to explain?

checklist.label: Thinking and communication change
checklist.question: Has it become harder to organize your thoughts or explain them to people?

checklist.label: Change from earlier functioning
checklist.question: What has changed in your routines, motivation or relationships?

checklist.label: Active and quieter periods
checklist.question: When did changes begin, and were there stretches when they eased?

checklist.label: Mood, substances and medical causes
checklist.question: How do these experiences relate to mood episodes, sleep, medicines or physical illness?

test.name: SCID-5 clinical interview
test.purpose: Clinician-led differential assessment of psychotic symptoms and their longitudinal course.
test.interpretation: Requires trained administration and appropriate materials; this educational checklist is not SCID and produces no diagnostic score.

cautions: Seek prompt assessment for new psychosis; urgent danger or inability to meet basic needs takes priority. Do not equate schizophrenia with violence or dissociative identity disorder.

sources.title: APA — What is schizophrenia? Related psychotic conditions
NIMH — Understanding psychosis
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Schizophreniform disorder
course: A schizophrenia-like episode lasts at least one month but less than six months; reassessment is needed as its course becomes clear.

checklist.label: Dated onset and duration
checklist.question: What was the first clear change, and when did it happen?

checklist.label: Psychotic experiences and organization
checklist.question: Which experiences or changes in thinking have been hardest to manage?

checklist.label: Baseline and current function
checklist.question: How are daily activities different from before this started?

checklist.label: Mood versus psychosis timeline
checklist.question: Do unusual experiences occur when your mood feels usual too?

checklist.label: Substances, sleep and medical history
checklist.question: What medication, substance, sleep or health changes happened around the onset?

differentials: Schizophrenia if sufficient course is established

test.name: SCID-5 clinical interview
test.purpose: Clinician-led differential assessment of psychosis with explicit duration review.
test.interpretation: Requires trained administration and appropriate materials; this educational checklist is not SCID and produces no diagnostic score.

cautions: Functional decline is clinically relevant but is not required in the same way as schizophrenia. Do not predict eventual schizophrenia from a short simulation.

sources.title: APA — What is schizophrenia? Related psychotic conditions
SAMHSA — DSM-IV to DSM-5 psychotic disorders comparison
NIMH — Understanding psychosis
Columbia University, SCID developer laboratory — SCID-5

name: Brief psychotic disorder
course: Psychosis lasts at least one day and less than one month, followed by full return to prior functioning; incomplete recovery leaves the formulation provisional.

checklist.label: Sudden change and trigger context
checklist.question: What happened around the day these experiences began?

checklist.label: Nature of the episode
checklist.question: What did you notice in your perceptions, beliefs or ability to communicate?

checklist.label: Duration and return to baseline
checklist.question: When did it stop, and what is still different from before?

checklist.label: Relationship to mood episodes
checklist.question: Were there sustained periods of very high or very low mood?

checklist.label: Medical and exposure review
checklist.question: Were there illnesses, medication changes, substances or severe sleep loss?

test.name: SCID-5 clinical interview
test.purpose: Clinician-led differential assessment of brief psychosis, recovery and exclusions.
test.interpretation: Requires trained administration and appropriate materials; this educational checklist is not SCID and produces no diagnostic score.
